nodes.html: Accountant fees in Australia vary depending on the service, complexity and expertise you need. Compare typical 2026 costs for individual tax returns, BAS, small business accounting, SMSF accounting and specialist advice — then get matched with a vetted accountant suited to your needs.

nodes.html: A straightforward individual return (one employer, no investments) typically costs $200–$400. Complexity pushes the price up: a rental property adds depreciation-schedule work ($350–$550), a CGT event from selling shares or property adds $300–$800, and trust distributions or foreign income can take a return to $600–$1,200. The matched agent quotes after reviewing your situation — the matching itself is free.

nodes.html: Ongoing small-business accounting typically runs $400–$1,000 per month for compliance. BAS preparation alone is usually $250–$400 per quarter depending on transaction volume. Catch-up work (overdue BAS or multiple years behind) is quoted separately and can be higher. Payroll-heavy businesses and those with inventory tend toward the top of the range.

nodes.html: Annual SMSF accounting and audit typically ranges from $1,500 to $3,500 — more if the fund holds property, has borrowings (LRBA) or needs Division 296 modelling. Specialist work like audit & assurance, business valuation or growth advisory is usually quoted as a fixed fee or monthly retainer ($500–$3,000+/month for advisory).

nodes.html: What drives the price — and how to control it
nodes.text: What drives the price — and how to control it

nodes.html: Three things move the price: complexity (entities, investments, structures), the state of your records (clean books cost less to process), and the credential required (a CPA-signed audit report costs more than a routine return). The biggest lever you control is record-keeping — tidy, reconciled books mean a faster, cheaper engagement. Matching to the right credential (not over-buying) is the second.
